subject: A little problem with a for enviroment in a reactive context

messages.author: 0d524fa2d2e56860
messages.subject: A little problem with a for enviroment in a reactive context
parts:
Hello

I have a little problem when using a for enviroment in my server.R. I'm new in Shiny so it may not be so complicated but I don't really understand what's happening.

I have a dataframe called mydata which is refreshed depending on the inputs. I want to create a newvariable from a variable depending on its value. Besides, mydata also contains a variable called ID. If the value of the variable equals to 'A', I want my newvariable to take a distinct value from the list of observations which have the same ID. In this example, I try to asign the value of the first element of that list.

 
   newvariable<-reactive(mydata()$variable})
  
     for(i in 1:nrow(mydata())){
      
          if(mydata()$variable[i]=='A'){
            
           othervalues<-reactive({ which( mydata()$ID==mydata()$ID[i]  & mydata()$variable!='A') });
           
           newvariable()[i] <- reactive ({ mydata()$variable[ othervalues()[1] ] })
           
           }
     
     }


And I get this error:

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)


Any help is appreciated. Thanks in advance!
